note: Read 2026-10-30: décret n° 2004-13 du 19 janvier 2004 fixant les règles d'application de la loi n° 2002-30 du 24 décembre 2002 portant Code de la route (partie réglementaire), in the text vie-publique.sn hosts (a Senegalese public-affairs site, not the Journal officiel itself, whose jo.gouv.sn didn't answer; marked secondary). Article 93: the licence is issued by the Directeur des Transports terrestres. Article 94: category B covers cars of up to eight passenger seats and goods vehicles up to 3,500 kg. Article 95: the minimum age of candidates for category B is 18; the decree sets no learner's or provisional licence, so 18 is the full licence's age. Article 97: a licence is granted on a medical certificate and for ten years for drivers under 45 (three years from 45 to 55, two years past 55), its validity extended by the Director on a new certificate at the end of each period; held as 10 years, the term for a first licence taken under 45 (the shorter terms past 45 the form doesn't hold, and they aren't an age the licence ends at). No fee is set in the decree and none was found from the Direction des Transports routiers (its sites didn't answer): fee null. Whether the decree has been amended on these articles since 2004 wasn't established (the Journal officiel didn't answer). No identity card is issued by the office; exchange (article on licences issued abroad, to be set by arrêté) not held.
